I've been on a quest to improve the air assist on my FSL 40W since it does make a huge difference in cutting ability. I've been using the stock air compressor for four years now, but it wasn't until a few months ago I discovered an air leak at the fittings where the air comes into the laser enclosure. It seems to be a design issue so I'm sure it was leaking from day one. I fixed that and improved my airflow. I then took some of the sharp bends out of the air hose leading to to the cutter head and improved it more. It helped a lot, but some experiments with even higher air flow gave me the ability to cut 1/4" plywood in one pass! That's a big improvement from the 3-4 passes I usually need to do. Unfortunately I can't run with this high airflow configuration normally. I bypassed the last 90 degree air fitting at the lens assembly to get more air, but now the lens doesn't have cooling or positive air pressure to keep vapors from getting on it. I need to design a new setup that takes the 90 degree bend out which cuts my airflow by about 50%. Maybe something I can change the airflow to match the job/material since air assist is great for cutting but can hinder engraving. I think that will be my weekend project. Thanks for the inspiration!
